title: Evals in Python: pytest gates, judge maths and tracing
seriesDescription: Retrieval metrics, pytest eval gates and guardrail code in Python. JEE-Advanced style: integer, assertion-reason, matrix match, fill-in-the-blanks, short code and multi-correct questions.
description: Python tooling for LLM evaluation: pytest regression gates and red-team tests, pass@k and Cohen kappa functions, percentile arithmetic, OpenTelemetry spans, and the Ragas, DeepEval and Langfuse roles.
source: pytest docs (parametrize, exit codes); Python statistics and math docs, all run locally; Zheng et al. MT-Bench (NeurIPS 2023); Codex paper (Chen et al.); Ragas, DeepEval and Langfuse docs; OpenTelemetry Python docs

questions.prompt: Write a pytest test named test_golden_pass_rate that calls run_eval() (it returns a list of dicts, each with a boolean key "passed") and fails the build if the pass rate is below 0.9.

checks.label: divides by the number of results

questions.model:
def test_golden_pass_rate():
    results = run_eval()
    rate = sum(r["passed"] for r in results) / len(results)
    assert rate >= 0.9, f"pass rate {rate:.0%}"
questions.explanation: Other forms pass (`statistics.mean`, numpy, asserting on a precomputed number of failures). Put a message in the assert so the CI log says what failed.

questions.prompt: Write a parametrized pytest that loads a list of cases from golden.json (each has "id", "question" and "expected_contains") and, for each, asserts that answer(question) contains expected_contains ignoring case. Use the case id as the test id.
questions.explanation: Each case becomes its own test, so the CI report names the exact failing case. Other correct forms (re.search with IGNORECASE) pass.

questions.prompt: Match each tool or technique to its role.

right.text: RAG metrics such as faithfulness, answer relevancy and context precision/recall
Unit-test-style LLM metrics (for example G-Eval) that run under pytest
Tracing plus datasets, scores and LLM-as-judge evaluators in a UI
Test runner whose exit code gates the CI pipeline

questions.explanation: Tools overlap, so describe the role you need (metrics, test harness, observability) and pick accordingly.

questions.prompt: In Python with OpenTelemetry, write a function `call_llm(prompt)` that runs inside a span named `"llm.call"` (use a tracer from `trace.get_tracer`) and sets a span attribute `"llm.model"` to `MODEL` before calling `client.generate(prompt)`.
questions.starter:
from opentelemetry import trace
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)

checks.label: opens the span as a context manager

questions.explanation: `start_as_current_span` ends the span and records exceptions for you. A decorator or `start_span` with try/finally also works but is more verbose; this check expects the context-manager form. The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions standardise attribute names such as `gen_ai.request.model` (still in development), so prefer those over invented keys like `llm.model` in real code.

questions.prompt: ATTACKS is a list of prompt-injection strings and SECRET is the system-prompt secret. Write a parametrized pytest test_no_leak that calls chatbot(prompt) and asserts SECRET never appears in the reply.
questions.explanation: Red-team prompts become regression tests: every new jailbreak you find is appended to ATTACKS. Also test paraphrased or encoded leaks, since exact-string checks miss base64 or translated output.

questions.prompt: Write pass_at_k(n, c, k) in Python for n sampled runs of which c passed: return 1 - C(n - c, k) / `C(n, k)` using math.comb, and 1.0 when fewer than k runs failed.
questions.explanation: I ran `pass_at_k(10, 3, 2)` = 0.5333, matching the earlier integer question. When fewer than k samples failed, every group of k contains a pass, so the answer is 1.0 (math.comb would also return 0 there, but the guard states the intent).

questions.prompt: Write cohen_kappa(human, judge) for two equal-length lists of labels: observed agreement po, chance agreement pe (the sum over labels of the share each rater gave it, multiplied), and return (po - pe) / (1 - pe).
questions.explanation: With 100 answers where the human labels 50 pass and 50 fail and the judge agrees on 90, I ran it and got 0.8, the figure from the earlier integer question. If both raters use one label only, pe is 1 and the division fails, so guard that case.

questions.prompt: A test function is decorated with `@pytest.mark.parametrize('a', [1, 2, 3])` and also with `@pytest.mark.parametrize('b', ['x', 'y'])`. How many test cases does pytest generate for it?
questions.explanation: Stacked parametrize marks multiply: 3 x 2 = 6 cases, one for each combination. I confirmed it with pytest --collect-only. Remember this when a matrix of prompts times models multiplies your LLM bill.

questions.prompt: Assertion and reason: read both statements and choose the right option.
questions.assertion: A CI job fails the build when a pytest golden-case test fails.
questions.reason: pytest exits with a non-zero status when any test fails, and CI treats a non-zero exit status as a failed step.

whys.a: Both true, and R explains A: the exit status is the signal the CI system reads.
whys.b: Not chosen: the exit status is exactly the mechanism by which the failure reaches CI.
whys.c: Not chosen: R is true; pytest returns a non-zero code on failures.
whys.d: Not chosen: A is true, a failing test fails the job.

questions.explanation: That is why an eval gate can be an ordinary test: assert on the pass rate and let the exit code carry the verdict.

questions.prompt: Which expression returns the 95th percentile of a list latencies using only the standard library?

options.why: Right: n=20 returns 19 cut points, and the 19th (index 18) is the 95th percentile.
This raises `IndexError`: only 19 cut points (indexes 0 to 18) are returned for n=20.
The median is the 50th percentile; scaling it by 0.95 is not a percentile.
An arbitrary offset; the index must come from the percentile, not a magic number.

questions.explanation: I ran it on 1..100 and got 95.95 (the default exclusive method). `numpy.percentile(latencies, 95)` is the common alternative when NumPy is available.

questions.prompt: Complete the pytest vocabulary for an eval suite.
questions.text: A {1} marker runs one test function once per golden case, a {2} shares an expensive object such as a judge client between tests, and a non-zero exit status from {3} fails the CI step.
questions.explanation: Keep fixtures scoped (session or module) for clients and datasets so the suite stays fast, and load golden cases from a versioned file.
